Bill Sikes. The brutal, violent burglar in Oliver Twist who serves as Fagin's enforcer and Nancy's abuser, embodying brute force and animal cruelty within the criminal underworld. A powerful, muscular criminal who specializes in housebreaking, he uses violence to maintain control over the gang and his paramour Nancy. He keeps a vicious mastiff as a constant companion, a reflection of his own brutish nature. When he discovers that Nancy has informed the authorities of their hideout, he beats her to death in a rage, committing the novel's most horrific act of cruelty. Pursued by guilt and a vengeful mob after Nancy's murder, he is haunted by visions of her bloodied face. He effectively engineers his own death by accident while attempting to escape. In later theatrical adaptations, his dog famously dies with him in the famous scene of his flight across rooftops. His story represents Dickens' conviction that violence and cruelty inevitably generate their own destruction and retribution.
